reason: The actual postgame entrance still has 100% Zubat, so its ordinary encounters offer little reason to revisit.
recommendation: Give the default table a mixed cave colony of Zubat, Woobat, Sableye and Wobbuffet; keep Zubat common and retain the selector alternatives as alternatives for this one area.

reason: Useful evolved catches and excellent Rock Smash rewards share most of their land roster with the basement.
recommendation: Make Shiinotic, Swoobat and Wobbuffet the common 1F residents by reusing the Druddigon, Lucario and Gigalith land slots; those displaced catches remain in the equally accessible basement wing.

reason: Guzzlord, Eelektross and Feebas reward exploration, but the water methods mix generic river residents with sea predators.
recommendation: Keep the special land finds; replace surface Swanna with Eelektross and Good Rod Sharpedo/Octillery with Whiscash/Quagsire to establish a subterranean pool.

reason: Smeargle now dominates at 56%, with useful cave companions that preserve a clear entrance identity.
A 54% Smeargle colony and stronger Sableye/Mawile presence make the narrower basement roster distinct and practical.
Fire-adapted woodland species, large insects and powerful forest curiosities give this side trip both identity and substantial rewards.
The gem, metal and dragon families fit well, although its bats and mineral residents do not establish a clear common anchor.
recommendation: Replace the Golbat slot with Sableye and the common Noibat slot with Mawile; keep the technological and dragon discoveries and their existing earliest access.

reason: Walking Wake gives this chamber a memorable discovery, but most ordinary residents repeat the entrance.
recommendation: Keep Walking Wake at its current chance; replace Boldore with an additional Glimmora slot and Noivern with an additional Goodra slot to emphasize the living depths.

reason: This connected optional floor contains only species already encountered in the entrance or 1F.
recommendation: Give the first optional floor a raw-mineral population led by Glimmet, Tinkatink and Duraludon; reuse its repeated bat and generic-dragon slots while preserving those catches on the earlier floors.

reason: Archaludon is useful, but this floor otherwise shares eleven of twelve species with 1F.
recommendation: Make Glimmora, Tinkatuff and Archaludon common in this mineral-maturation floor by repeating them in the Boldore, Noivern and Druddigon slots.

reason: Clefable and Metang provide some separation, but most of the final approach repeats the preceding optional floor.
recommendation: Increase Clefable and Metang using the repeated Noivern and Druddigon slots, and replace Boldore with Carbink to lead naturally into the crystal room.

reason: Carbink at 57% and three coherent mineral companions make the chamber immediately recognizable.
Ditto, unusual fossil combinations and three-segment Dudunsparce are excellent discoveries, while Flittle feels detached from the buried habitat.
recommendation: Replace Flittle with a second Ditto slot to strengthen the unusual underground colony while retaining every fossil and the rare Dudunsparce form.

reason: Blacephalon, Blaze Tauros and fire specialists make the detour rewarding, with a little generic cave filler.
recommendation: Replace Noibat with an extra Magcargo slot and Boldore with Coalossal to make the ordinary population reflect the volcanic corridor.

reason: Torkoal, Magby, Charcadet and Slither Wing support demanding teams while the soot, heat and burrowing species fit the passage.
Cliff dwellers and strong dragons give useful options, though the scattered roster lacks a dominant mountain resident.
recommendation: Replace the Fearow slot with Gligar to reinforce the cliff habitat; preserve every current dragon and the useful early catches.

reason: The volcano roster is useful and coherent, but its common cave species do little to distinguish the hideout entrance.
recommendation: Replace Geodude and Zubat with additional Numel and Slugma slots, retaining the stronger fire and ground options in their existing slots.

reason: Ten of twelve species repeat 1F, with Geodude/Zubat merely exchanged for Graveler/Noibat.
recommendation: Make this the excavated tunnel room by repeating Drilbur and Excadrill in the Numel and Slugma slots; keep its fire catches available on the entrance floor.

reason: Koffing, Grimer and their fire companions already suggest an industrial pollution pocket.
recommendation: Replace Noibat with a second Grimer slot to strengthen the room’s pollution identity while retaining Weezing, Houndoom and Salandit.

reason: Houndour and Salandit families offer a predator theme, but generic cave residents dilute it.
recommendation: Replace Noibat with Houndour and Graveler with Salandit, retaining Camerupt and both evolved predators.

reason: The evolved volcanic population and Volcarona are useful, but Noibat remains a large generic interruption.
recommendation: Replace the 11% Noibat slot with Camerupt to make the deep volcanic population unmistakable.

reason: Eleven of twelve species repeat the previous chamber despite the useful Chandelure addition.
recommendation: Repeat Weezing and Magcargo in the Noibat and Excadrill slots to make this a distinct fume-and-lava pocket; preserve its evolved fire discoveries.

reason: The roster is useful but overlaps heavily with both neighboring third-floor rooms.
recommendation: Use the Noibat and Weezing slots for extra Larvesta and Heatmor, giving this chamber a recognizable heat-adapted insect population.

reason: Gouging Fire and a fully capable volcanic roster reward reaching the bottom.
recommendation: Replace Weezing with an extra Coalossal slot to emphasize the hottest cavern while retaining Gouging Fire and every current evolved fire option.

reason: Celestial rocks and dragon prospects make excellent land encounters, but Lombre and Lanturn dilute the cave-pool fishing identity.
recommendation: Keep the land roster; replace Super Rod Lombre and Lanturn with Slowbro and Whiscash to align fishing with the existing cave pool.

reason: Scream Tail makes the chamber worthwhile, while the water methods mostly repeat a generic river selection.
recommendation: Keep Scream Tail and Feebas; replace Super Rod Seaking and Poliwhirl with Whiscash and Crawdaunt so this pool has a clearer resident population.

reason: The new Dratini/Dragonair/Kingdra surface population gives the room a strong dragon-pool identity that fishing only partly supports.
recommendation: Replace Super Rod Sharpedo and Octillery with Dragonair and Dratini, preserving Kingdra’s current slot.

reason: Roaring Moon, Salamence and Dragonite make the land roster excellent, but the water loses the dragon identity of the preceding room.
recommendation: Keep every land discovery; replace surface Lombre with Dragonair and Super Rod Lombre/Golduck with Kingdra/Dragonair.

reason: The Beldum line, metal specialists and unusual powerful finds create a distinctive and useful reward chamber.
The sandy entry offers varied relic, desert and strong battle options immediately, with clear discoveries on adjoining floors.
Dwebble, Orthworm and Krokorok distinguish it somewhat, but the common population still resembles the entry.
recommendation: Replace the repeated Bronzor slot with Baltoy and the repeated Golett slot with Dwebble to emphasize moving sand and creatures in the masonry.

reason: Golurk, Bronzong and Claydol create useful progression, although the common Yamask and Darumaka repeat the lower floors.
recommendation: Replace the Yamask slot with Claydol to make the animated relics the main residents, preserving Darumaka and the remaining battle options.

reason: Cofagrigus and Bronzong now have real presence, while Darmanitan and Krookodile remain satisfying summit catches.
Gimmighoul is a strong treasury discovery, but the ordinary population still closely echoes the sandy entrance.
recommendation: Keep Gimmighoul, Gabite and Spiritomb in their current slots; reuse the Sandshrew and Trapinch slots for Bronzor and Golett to make this a buried vault.

reason: Duskull and Shuppet now lead clearly, and the varied ghost roles remain easy enough to find.
Antique Sinistea is a distinctive find, but most ordinary encounters repeat 1F.
recommendation: Replace the Gastly and Haunter slots with extra Phantump and Murkrow, preserving Antique Sinistea at its present chance.

reason: Litwick and Lampent together establish a candle-filled floor without losing the tower’s signature ghost families.
Banette and Dusclops each reach 20%, with Mimikyu and evolved ghost options giving the upper tower a clear payoff.
Artisan Poltchageist and Drifblim differentiate the floor, but Noibat remains conspicuous filler.
recommendation: Replace Noibat with a second Drifblim slot, keeping Artisan Poltchageist and all evolved ghost discoveries.

reason: The concentrated evolved-ghost roster now makes the final floor feel like a culmination, with practical chances throughout.
Ritual, guardian and regional ghost choices suit the mountain, with Beheeyem the least connected resident.
recommendation: Replace Beheeyem with an extra Chimecho slot; Beheeyem remains on the summit and the regional ghosts keep their existing access.

reason: Flutter Mane, ominous regional ghosts and evolved mountain residents make the summit distinct and rewarding.
A coherent electrical and machinery ecosystem supplies support, offense and unusual discoveries without weakening Magnemite’s association.
Iron Hands rewards entering, but ten of twelve species repeat the entrance and Wattrel adds little generator identity.
recommendation: Replace Wattrel with an extra Magnemite slot and Porygon2 with an extra Tynamo slot, retaining Iron Hands and the rest of the current options.

reason: Great Tusk, Unown and animated relics reward the maze, while Swanna and Octillery make its water feel generic.
recommendation: Keep the land discoveries; replace surface Swanna with Gastrodon and Good Rod Octillery with Barboach to reinforce an excavated desert pool.

reason: Iron Treads and Orthworm give this physical branch an excellent mechanical-burrower theme, but Rock Smash repeats the other ruins.
recommendation: Replace Rock Smash Baltoy with Orthworm and Onix with Dwebble, retaining Steelix and the current land discoveries.

reason: The actual exit-side floor repeats evolved relics already available in B1F and adds little encounter identity.
recommendation: Make Sigilyph and Claydol the common exit-side guardians using the repeated Yamask and Bronzong slots; retain Darmanitan, Krookodile and the strong relic options.

reason: Cofagrigus and Golurk now anchor the chamber, while Stakataka, Aegislash and practical Rock Smash finds reward the maze.
The volcanic entrance is dominated by generic cave species, and its Super Rod roster exactly repeats Route102.
recommendation: Repeat Magmar and Heatmor in the Noibat and Machoke slots; use Slowbro, Whiscash, Gastrodon, Quagsire and Dratini for a distinct cave-pool Super Rod roster.

reason: Iron Moth and the fire specialists reward the descent, though repeated bats and generic cave fighters soften the volcanic identity.
recommendation: Replace Noibat with Coalossal and Gurdurr with Turtonator, keeping Iron Moth and the stronger current discoveries.

reason: The chamber has fitting fire species, but ordinary rocks and burrowers occupy enough space to make it resemble the preceding floor.
recommendation: Replace Boldore with an extra Larvesta slot and Dugtrio with Magcargo so the hottest room has a recognizable resident population.

reason: Ghosts and ancient constructs suit the lower ruin, but its Sableye/Mawile opening feels borrowed from other caves.
recommendation: Repeat Claydol and Golurk in the Sableye and Mawile slots, keeping the dragons and celestial finds.

reason: Dragonair, Salamence and Metagross supply useful progression, but common ghosts still dominate the elevated floor.
recommendation: Replace Banette with an extra Altaria slot to make airborne residents more prominent while preserving the evolved discoveries.

reason: Ten of twelve species repeat 3F, so the final inhabited floor scarcely develops the skyward climb.
recommendation: Repeat Minior and Altaria in the Banette and Claydol slots, retaining Dusknoir, Drakloak, Salamence and Metagross.

reason: The entrance offers excellent final-team options, though its collection of cave and championship species lacks a dominant local resident.
recommendation: Replace Noibat with an extra Medicham slot to give the entrance a stronger training-ground identity while preserving every fully evolved headliner.

reason: Iron Jugulis and Rock Smash Tyranitar are valuable, but eleven of twelve land species repeat 1F.
recommendation: Repeat Iron Jugulis and Metagross in the Noivern and Medicham slots so the basement has a distinct dark-and-metal emphasis; preserve the other strong options and Rock Smash rewards.

reason: The land roster repeats earlier floors, and its generic river methods provide little final-cavern identity.
recommendation: Repeat Kommo-o and Dragapult in the Noibat and Medicham slots; replace surface Seaking/Shellos with Slowbro/Gastrodon and exchange the Super Rod Drednaw/Dragonair positions to emphasize the dragon pool.
